title: Keyless Entry Rear Antenna: Removal and Installation
introduction:
The rear antenna sits behind the luggage-compartment scuff plate, the trim across the loading edge. I use that trim as the landmark: uncover the mounting area, disconnect the antenna, then release its retainers. Knowing which piece provides access saves turning a small electrical job into a trim-wrestling contest.

The drawings show a coupe; the convertible procedure is similar. This guide covers removal and refitting, rather than diagnosing a keyless-entry fault.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Eye, ear and hand protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged components. Failure to use the applicable protection may result in serious personal injury. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

edits.text: NOTE: The illustrations show a coupe. Removal and installation on a convertible are similar.
edits.why: Use the drawings to identify the luggage-compartment trim and antenna mounting area while retaining the body-style qualification.

edits.text: Open the luggage compartment lid to reach the trim across the loading edge.
edits.why: The opening provides access to the scuff plate covering the antenna mounting area.

edits.text: Remove the luggage compartment scuff plate using the retainer and lifting steps below.
edits.why: This is the trim panel across the rear edge of the luggage-compartment opening, around the central latch opening.

edits.text: Unscrew and remove the thumb nut type retainers securing the luggage compartment scuff plate.
edits.why: The inset identifies the retainers near the ends of the panel. Freeing them first allows the trim to come away without pulling against its attachments.

edits.text: Lift the luggage compartment scuff plate upward from the loading edge and remove it.
edits.why: The upward arrows show the removal movement. With the trim out, the antenna mounting area is exposed.

edits.text: NOTE: The luggage compartment lid is omitted from the antenna illustration for clarity; removing the lid is not part of this procedure.
edits.why: The drawing gives an unobstructed view of the mounting area without adding a lid-removal operation.

edits.text: Remove the keyless entry rear antenna from behind the scuff-plate area by disconnecting its electrical connector and releasing its retainers as described below.
edits.why: I use the close-up to distinguish the small rectangular antenna from the surrounding bodywork and wiring.

edits.text: Disconnect the electrical connector plugged into the end of the keyless entry rear antenna.
edits.why: Disconnecting the wiring before freeing the antenna prevents the harness from becoming its accidental tether.

edits.text: Remove the push-in retainers at the antenna mounting tabs, then remove the keyless entry rear antenna from the rear body panel.
edits.why: The close-up identifies the retaining locations and shows the push-in retainer profile, distinguishing these attachments from the scuff plate's threaded retainers.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: position the rear antenna on its mounting points, install its retainers and reconnect its electrical connector. Refit the luggage compartment scuff plate over the loading edge and install its thumb nut type retainers.
edits.why: Before covering the antenna, check that its retainers hold it and its electrical connector is fully seated. After the scuff plate is secured, remove tools and loose parts, keep everyone clear of the lid and close it. For an ordinary operation check, leave the engine and ignition OFF, keep the car in its parked gear with the parking brake applied, and keep your intelligent access key with you outside the car at the rear opening. Press the exterior luggage-release button hidden above the license plate; the lid should unlatch. Open it, then close and latch it again before driving. Keep the key outside the luggage compartment throughout—this is not the moment to test your talent for locking yourself out. This checks the disturbed luggage-release operation, not the rear antenna in isolation or the cause of an earlier fault. If operation is abnormal, stop and use the matching keyless-entry diagnosis; do not treat repeated parts swapping as a test. Leave the ignition OFF, the parking brake applied and the parked gear selected when finished; keep the key outside the car before any connector reinspection. See the [matching owner manual, Locks: luggage compartment](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/Catalog/owner_information/2015-Mustang-Owners-Manual-version-1_om_EN-US_07_2014.pdf) for these ordinary release controls and the close-and-latch precaution.

editorialRevision.scope: Replace generic startup preparation with already reviewed stationary known-state owner setup; add ordinary exterior luggage-release operation after full reassembly, explicitly not antenna isolation or fault diagnosis. Primary text, figures, source refs and specifications unchanged. Independent incremental approval recorded separately.
